CHIEF COMPLAINT
Anxiety and breast concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Donna Torres is a 45-year-old female presenting for follow-up. Patient reports that her anxiety has improved significantly with Buspar, which was recently started by Dr. Brown. She experienced severe anxiety in November and December that would typically start during the day at work. Patient notes that the week before her period, her anxiety would spike, but this later evolved into random anxiety episodes. She was started on Singulair by Dr. Ward during this timeframe, and acknowledges that Singulair can cause anxiety as a side effect. Patient reports she was also on progesterone during this period for menstrual regulation. Patient attributes some of her anxiety to work-related stress, including leading the process of delivering COVID results to patients and supporting the opening of evaluation centers and a COVID clinic during the pandemic. She felt guilty for experiencing anxiety while not being on the frontlines. Since stopping Camila birth control, patient notes her hunger level has decreased significantly; she had been eating constantly while on the medication. Patient reports some weight loss over the past six months. Regarding breast concerns, patient notes that breast lumps she had previously are smaller but still present. She reports tenderness in the left breast, particularly in an area where she had previously developed a clog while breastfeeding. Patient continues to experience itching or discomfort in the pelvic area and uses prescribed cream once weekly with good response; she needs a refill. Patient denies other issues.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current weight loss concerns. Denies abnormal vaginal symptoms beyond previous itching/discomfort now well-controlled with topical cream. No pelvic pain or other complaints noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Anxiety (recently diagnosed)
Menstrual irregularity
Breast lumps/fibrocystic changes
Previous abnormal Pap smear in 2009 (required surveillance for six months, then normalized)
History of clogged milk duct while breastfeeding

MEDICATIONS
Buspar (recently started by Dr. Brown for anxiety)
Progesterone (for menstrual regulation)
Topical cream for vulvar itching/discomfort (using once weekly)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 45.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in healthcare setting with responsibility for patient communication and pandemic-related workflow management. Received COVID-19 vaccine. Husband and daughter have not yet received COVID-19 vaccine; patient reports ongoing discussions at home regarding vaccine hesitancy. Son has received first dose of COVID-19 vaccine. Breastfeeding history noted.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal respirations.
Neck: Small nodules palpated; patient notes these are smaller than previously noted. No acute concern.
Breast Examination: Left breast feels slightly denser than right. Tenderness noted on left breast in lower region where patient previously had clogged duct. Lumps palpable bilaterally, smaller than previous examination but still present.
Pelvic Examination: External genitalia appear normal. No acute abnormalities noted.

RESULTS
Pap smear: Last performed in 2019, negative for dysplasia and infection. Previous abnormal Pap in 2009 required six-month surveillance, subsequently normalized. Repeat Pap smear ordered today given patient's history and physician's concern regarding potential increase in abnormal findings related to immunocompromise, stress, and vaccination status.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Well-controlled on Buspar. Continue current therapy. Consider possible hormonal contribution. Monitor response.

2. Breast lumps/fibrocystic changes: Lumps have decreased in size since previous examination but remain palpable. No change in examination suggests benign etiology. Reassured patient regarding benign nature of cysts, fibroadenomas, and other breast issues. Patient expresses concern given age (nearly 40) and mother's history of breast cancer diagnosed at 45. Referral placed to breast specialist for further evaluation and surveillance. Breast specialist will provide in-office ultrasound as extension of physical exam and can perform procedures if needed more expediently than radiology. Specialist will contact patient within 2 business days to schedule.

3. Pap smear: Last Pap in 2019 was negative. Repeat Pap ordered today given history of abnormal Pap in 2009 and physician's concern regarding potential increased abnormal findings in context of immunocompromise and stress.

4. Vulvar itching/discomfort: Well-controlled on topical cream used once weekly. Refill prescribed.

5. Medications: Discontinuation of Camila birth control associated with improved appetite and weight loss, which patient tolerating well. Continue progesterone for menstrual regulation.
